- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for risk-off or panic-driven rebounds.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or apply decay factor to subsequent days.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from peak), model often fails to recognize it; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-peak.  
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent trends; if history shows high volatility or sentiment swings, reduce forecast smoothness and add 1–2% downward buffer.  
- When sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” values, model underperforms; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for suppressed market sentiment.
